Start with the setup notebook, then follow the modules in order. Every notebook loads its own data from this repository, so you can open any of them cold, with two exceptions: Lab 10 starts from Lab 9's preference data and reward model, which are [not built yet](readiness.qmd#open-work), and Lab 12's comparison with Lab 11 uses a file that Lab 11 writes.

{{< include /_includes/notebooks.md >}}

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
Notebooks are stored without outputs. Work through the cells one at a time. **Runtime → Run all** stops at the first exercise you have not written, which is the point: to see a whole lab run, tick `WORKED_EXAMPLE` in the harness cell first.
:::

## How the labs are laid out

- **Setup cell.** Installs and imports. Run it first.
- **Exercises.** Each has a `# TODO` cell for you to complete.
- **Harness.** The first code cell. Run it first; it keeps the solutions from replacing your code. Tick `WORKED_EXAMPLE` in it to run the whole lab as a worked example instead.
- **Solutions.** Folded directly beneath each exercise. Try the exercise first, then open the solution to compare. Running a solution cell stores the reference; it does not overwrite your function.
- **Checkpoints.** A cell after each exercise that passes or fails and says whose code it checked: yours or the reference. If you are stuck, run exercise N's folded solution cell, then `workshop.use_reference(N)`, and go on with the reference solution.
- **Summary.** The last code cell lists which checkpoints passed on your own code.
- **Stretch.** An optional final section. Nothing later depends on it.

API keys are optional. See [Setup](setup.qmd).
